acceptance.output_evidence: _nearest_price now has exactly one resolving branch (on_or_before non-empty -> max by date) and one UNRESOLVED branch (empty on_or_before -> None); the either-direction fallback (`min(price_series, key=lambda t: abs(...))`) is deleted entirely, not merely guarded, so there is no code path left that can return a price dated after period_end. gap_days is (period_end - price_date).days with no abs(), so a bug that reintroduced a future price would surface as a NEGATIVE gap_days rather than silently passing an under-45-day check -- the invariant is now structurally visible, not just behaviorally enforced. The direction assertion (test_fiscal_period_join_direction_assertion_all_landed_securities) reads price_date <= period_end off fiscal_period_join's own output rows (the production join, not a synthetic reimplementation) across all 3 already-landed securities -- December filers (SAP GY, BA US) via their own annual series and the non-December filer (BABA US) via its dense DAILY series -- and additionally checks gap_days >= 0 on every resolved row, which the removed abs() could previously have masked. The negative control (test_nearest_price_future_only_returns_unresolved) reproduces the exact CVO scenario (@b3acbcf3dd: period_end 2025-12-31, only 2026-01-02 at price 100) and asserts None; a companion test confirms the ordinary on-or-before case still resolves correctly (no regression). Left to the CVO's judgment: whether UNRESOLVED (rather than e.g. a flagged/annotated future price) is the right SEMANTIC answer for downstream consumers, and whether checking 3 landed securities' resolved rows plus 1 synthetic negative control is a COMPLETE direction assertion or whether a wider synthetic battery (e.g. price exactly on period_end, price series entirely empty) should be demanded.
